description: “Boo! 👻 I’m Astro Boo, a little cosmic explorer with a big mission! 🌌✨ I love to code, create, explore, and turn curious ideas into fun solutions. From space to Earth, I believe technology should make life easier, kinder, and better for everyone. 💻🌍💜
summary:
Ignis: one consistent NASA fire record for Italy, from 2003 to today

NASA has mapped fires with MODIS since 2000 and with the sharper VIIRS since 2012. VIIRS detects 3.3 times more fire, so simply joining the two makes fire appear to jump in 2012. We built Ignis to fix this.

Both sensors are first counted the same way, as 5 km fire cell-days. Then an ensemble model is trained on 2012–2025, when both satellites flew. It combines a negative binomial equation for each region with gradient boosting driven by NASA POWER weather. The model converts every MODIS month before 2012 into what VIIRS would have seen, with an uncertainty band; we did the same for fire intensity. On years the model never saw, the yearly error is 2.6%. The false jump falls from ×1.85 to ×0.90, and agreement with NASA’s burned-area products (MCD64A1, VNP64A1) rises from 0.08 to 0.79. NOAA-20 keeps the record going after S-NPP.

The Ignis app uses this record for three groups:

Scientists: real trends, causes and fire types.
Fire responders: live fires, a 7-day risk forecast and landslide alerts on burned slopes.
Farmers: safe windows to burn, and booked burns that responders see as planned, not false alarms.

This matters because decisions need real fire trends, not sensor artefacts.
